content.title: About
content.content: Oolong is a semi‑oxidized tea made from the leaves of Camellia sinensis. It sits between green and black tea, offering a light fruity aroma and a gentle briskness. Served hot, it is typically brewed using whole leaves.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oolong originates from the Fujian province of China and Taiwan.
There are more than 30 varieties, each with distinct aromas ranging from floral to nutty.
The “twisting” technique of the leaves preserves natural flavors and makes brewing easier.
Oolong is often featured in tea ceremonies that value its evolving flavor profile over multiple infusions.
Aged oolongs, stored for several years, develop a deep, earthy character.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Oolong contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Metabolism boost
items.content: Caffeine and catechins may increase metabolic rate and aid fat oxidation.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Regular moderate consumption can help lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Stress reduction
items.content: Aromatic compounds in oolong have calming effects, promoting relaxation.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Warm oolong stimulates gastric juice production, easing digestion.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Oolong contains caffeine; those sensitive should limit intake.

items.title: Iron absorption
items.content: Tannins may reduce iron absorption, so avoid drinking tea with iron supplements.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergy to tea components.

items.title: Water quality
items.content: Hard water can alter flavor and increase mineral content in the brew.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour hot water (80‑90 °C) over the leaf oolong and steep for 2‑3 minutes. Multiple infusions are possible, extending steep time slightly each round. Drink plain or with a touch of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store oolong in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Keep it away from direct sunlight and moisture to prevent oxidation of the leaves.
